text:
Dear hiring manager,

I am writing to apply to the junior analyst position you published last week. I have twenty six years and I finished my degree in economics two years ago. Since three years I work in a small consulting office in Valencia, where I prepare monthly reports. During that time I assisted to many meetings with clients from the food industry. My manager asked me to realize a study of their delivery costs, and the result was very satisfactory for the whole team. I am agree with your idea that a good analyst must explain numbers in simple words.

In my present work I use spreadsheets every day, and actually I am learning the basics of Python. The people in my office is very kind, so I could ask them for help whenever a formula failed. I think the quality of a report depends of the questions you ask before you open the file. In the other hand, a clean table is useless when nobody reads it. That is why I always explain them my tables in a short call before I send the file. My colleagues say I am a sensible listener, and I take it as a compliment.

I would like to move to a bigger company because I want to learn more good methods of forecasting. Your job advertisement says the team works with retail data, and that interest me a lot. I can start in the first of September, and I do not need any relocation support. I pretend to bring the same care I give to my present clients. Thank you for reading my letter, and I stay at your disposal for any question.

I also want to mention my formation in statistics, because your advertisement asks for it. Last winter I follow an online course about regression models. The teacher give us a final project with real sales data, and my report received a good mark. Since that course I am reading one article about forecasting every week. I know theory alone is not enough, and for that I practise with the data of my own office. I can send you a short example of my work for email.

Kind regards,
Lucia
